verdict: Supermicro's sales jumped 55% to $5.7 billion, but thinner margins and surging costs left profit nearly flat at $321 million — and the figures were preliminary, reported while its audited filings were still months late.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted; flat vs $0.51 a year ago (non-GAAP $0.58–0.60 per the preliminary release)

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: vs 15.4% a year ago; non-GAAP gross margin 11.8–11.9% per the preliminary release

kpis.label: Cash and equivalents
kpis.note: vs approximately $1.9B of total debt at Dec 31, 2024, per the preliminary release

segments.name: Total net sales
segments.note: Supermicro reports a single operating segment and printed no product split for the quarter. Sales are mostly complete server and rack systems for AI and cloud data centers. Two customers each accounted for 10% or more of net sales in the quarter (Customer A 27.1% and Customer G 30.6%, per the 10-Q).

flow.revenueNote: Money from selling servers, racks and related systems to data-center customers.
flow.costOfRevenueNote: What it cost to build the servers and racks sold — mostly hardware components.
flow.grossProfitNote: Revenue left after the direct cost of the hardware — 11.8% of revenue, down from 15.4% a year ago.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing next-generation servers, racks and Data Center Building Block Solutions; up 45% YoY.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing; up 70% YoY as Supermicro chased larger data-center deals.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Back office, legal and facilities; up 71% YoY.

flow.operatingIncomeNote: $369M of operating income — $670M of gross profit minus $301M of operating expenses.
flow.otherIncomeNote: $13M of other income, net, less $7M of interest expense.
flow.taxNote: A $57M tax provision on $375M of pre-tax income, a 15.2% GAAP tax rate.
flow.netIncomeNote: The bottom line: $321M of net income, up 8% from $296M a year ago.

follow100Note: Supermicro keeps $5.65 of every $100 because the hardware itself costs $88.19 — its model is volume, not margin. Rows are rounded to the nearest cent; cost of revenue is rounded down a touch so the rounded rows sum exactly to the rounded profit of $5.65 per $100.

takeaways.title: Sales jumped, margins thinned
takeaways.text: Net sales hit $5,678M, up from $3,665M a year ago, but gross margin narrowed to 11.8% from 15.4% as hardware costs ate $5,008M of the total. Operating income was flat at $369M versus $371M a year ago.

takeaways.title: Profit barely grew
takeaways.text: Net income was $321M, up 8% from $296M a year ago, and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.51 — flat year over year. Operating expenses rose 56% to $301M, with R&D up 45%, sales and marketing up 70% and G&A up 71%.

takeaways.title: Preliminary numbers, delayed filings, guidance cut
takeaways.text: These figures were labeled preliminary — Supermicro's audited 10-K and 10-Qs were still unfiled when it reported, and the final 10-Q landed February 25, 2025. It also cut full-year FY25 revenue guidance to $23.5–25.0B from $26–30B, and disclosed DOJ and SEC subpoenas following a short-seller report.

otherDetail: Other income of $6.4M combines $13.0M of other income, net — mostly interest earned on investments and cash balances plus foreign-exchange gains — less $6.5M of interest expense. A separate $2.5M share of income from an equity investee is shown as equityM. Stock-based compensation was approximately $63.0M in the quarter, per the preliminary release; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.58–0.60 versus GAAP $0.51. Two customers each accounted for 10% or more of net sales: Customer A at 27.1% and Customer G at 30.6%.
footerNote: Q3 FY25 guidance: net sales $5.0–6.0B, GAAP EPS $0.36–0.53; FY25 revenue guidance cut to $23.5–25.0B from $26–30B.
pngFooterNote: Sales up 55% to $5.7B, but profit barely moved.
